label: COMMUNICATION

cover.headline: When your families *expect different things*
cover.sub: 5 ways to stay a team this season.

points.heading: Talk before the visits
points.body: Agree on plans in private before anyone else weighs in.
points.panel: “What matters most to you about seeing your family this year?”

points.heading: Each handle your own family
points.body: Hard news usually lands better from their own child.
points.panel: “Would you talk to your mom about the dates?”

points.heading: Trade, don’t keep score
points.body: One year here, one year there. Fairness over time works better.
points.panel: “Let’s alternate, and write it down so we remember.”

points.heading: Protect a little time for you two
points.body: Even a busy holiday can hold one quiet moment for just you.
points.panel: Plan a short walk together on each family day.

points.heading: Debrief kindly afterward
points.body: Share what went well first, then what to change next time.
points.panel: “What would you do differently next year?”

close.save: Save this before the next family visit.

caption:
Two families often means two sets of traditions, expectations, and opinions, especially in December.

You can’t please everyone. But you can face it together, agree in private first, and protect your marriage in the middle of it all. Here are five ways to stay on the same side.

Save this before the next family visit, and follow @spotseason for more.
